title: Resources
text:
Below are resources I have put together for eco-evolutionary modelling workshops I have run / contributed to. I hope they can be of further interest here.



Material
Description
Link




Eco-evolutionary modelling: gen3sis
An introductionary tutorial to gen3sis, an eco-evolutionary modelling framework for exploring the mechanisms underlying large-scale biodiversity patterns.
https://github.com/thomaskeggin/gen3sis_sandbox


Multilayer network analyses
A tutorial on how a multilayer network analysis approach can be implemented in spatiotemporal eco-evolutionary studies - both conceptually and methodologically.
https://github.com/melian009/muaux/tree/main/HandsOn/src/Thomas

title: Welcome
text:
I’m a biologist working to tackle contemporary biodiversity challenges through genetics, ecological observations, eco-evolutionary modelling, and theoretical development. I’m striving for a holistic understanding of biological systems, and spend most of my time being humbled by their complexity.
My latest work has been leading a collaboration to advance our methods and understanding of how tropical fishes might respond to climate change by moving, adapting, or going extinct. Check out our preprint here.
